finding:
Main prompts (scenes described) + the grid sentence (11:15 AM)

Rows av2_gridv_image_mgrid / av2_gridv_video_mgrid: the 20 main prompts, which describe a scene (lawn, beach, living room), with the grid sentence at the end, same model (grid + video LoRA). The grid sentence wins over the scene in most videos: 19 of 20 have background alpha 0.000, core 0.995. Where some scene survives (the dog's lawn, the horse's beach strip) it is drawn in the colour panels but left out of the matte, so the RGBA is the subject cut out of its scene (a low registration IoU there, 0.37 and 0.48, measures that disagreement, not a shifted layout). Failure: the cat (r10) starts as one full-frame living-room scene and becomes a grid later (seam off 180 px, background 0.22).

Unrequested variant (11:10 AM): alpha = max(4th panel, three-background alpha)

Not the user's spec (m01006: the three colours decontaminate, the 4th panel is the mask; that stays the headline above). Tested because the 4th panel drops thin, semi-transparent parts that the three background panels do show. Variant (layout grid2x2mix, h3magic/grid.py mix_alpha): alpha = max(4th-panel alpha, three-background alpha where that is ≥ 0.1); colour decontaminated with that alpha. No new renders: the rows av2_gridvmix_* are re-derived from the same frames as av2_gridv_* (same model, prompts and seeds).

By eye (images): the chef's flying vegetables and flame, the coffee stream, the cannonball splash and the wave's spray now come through in the RGBA, as semi-transparent parts. Numbers: images: missed subject 0.11% → 0 by construction; extra (solid alpha where the backgrounds see background) 0.81% both; videos: background alpha still 0.000 on 20/20 (per-prompt median; mean over all border pixels 0.041 vs 0.039), subject core 1.000. The |Δα| numbers of the variant are computed against its own mixed alpha and are not comparable. Cost: the splash and spray come with the three-background alpha's softness and its errors where the panels disagree (the cannonball's second child is translucent).

The grid video LoRA (10:40 AM): the best video model of Alpha Video v2

Why. Trained on still images only, the grid sometimes loses its layout in video: the cat starts as one full-frame cat, the candle's white panel turns black, the steam train's panels drift. Fix: a small LoRA (split_grid_video) trained on video with gray magic v3t and the grid LoRA baked in: 300 synthetic clips in which a MAGICK cut-out moves along a smooth random path for 39 frames, rendered exactly as 2×2 grids (gray, white / black, alpha) and tiled-encoded (table h3_motion_clips). Guidance loss 4, lr 1e-4, 250 steps on node 2's GPUs 0–3 (~11 s per step); validation 1.91 → 1.45 → 1.38 → 1.37 at steps 1 / 50 / 100 / 150.

"Background 0.000" alone can lie: a misplaced matte still has a clean background. At step 150 the cat's layout broke around frame 108 (the top panels end at y ≈ 310 instead of 384; the matte sits lower-left of the cat, so the RGBA shows a cut-off, see-through cat with purple fringes; frame below). The registration check (every 5th frame: IoU of the panel alpha vs the three-background alpha at the fixed panel boundaries, plus where the seams really are) catches it. At the final step no video has a moving seam; the 6 videos with some bad frames (cannonball splash 24%, cyclist 17%, wave 17%, basketball 10%, horse 10%, skater 3%) have the seams in place and IoU means 0.84–0.94: coarse mattes on splash, spokes and thin parts, not a shifted layout.

Colour. Colour is decontaminated with the panel alpha by the per-pixel median of the three foreground estimates F_k = (C_k − (1 − α)·b_k)/α (one inconsistent panel cannot wash the colour out). At video-LoRA step 100 the cat's white panel was drawn in a different pose (colour spread 0.54); at step 200 the panels agree (0.16).

Panel size (is 384 too small for thin parts?): a grid with 512-pixel panels (a 1024² frame, split_grid1024) at step 200 vs 384 panels at step 200: missed subject 0.22% vs 0.10%, IoU 0.933 vs 0.940, edge |Δα| 0.197 vs 0.179, and by eye it still leaves out the flying vegetables, the flame and the splash. So the panel size is not the bottleneck; training stopped there, and 1024² videos (4× the render cost) were not made.

Final grid split (step 456, 9:00 AM): images

Training stopped at step 456 (validation flat since step 250). Row av2_grid_image_fgrid (the 20 subject-only prompts + the grid sentence): missed subject 0.35%, extra 0.43%, IoU 0.922; |Δα| all pixels mean 0.028, median 0.007, 95th percentile 0.133; edge band mean 0.172, median 0.099, 95th percentile 0.589; subject core 0.999; background 0.000; fit residual 0.016.

By eye, compared with step 50: the coffee stream and most of the pot are now in the matte, the spinning top's hand is in all four panels and in the matte, the chef's wok and plate are in; the wave's spray is partly in. Still missing: the chef's flying vegetables and the flame, and the coffee steam (thin, semi-transparent parts): the panel alpha draws them as clear while the three backgrounds show them, so decontaminating with the panel alpha drops them. The worst prompts by missed share are the cannonball splash (1.9%), the hummingbird's flowers (1.4%) and the skater (1.3%).

Final grid split (step 456): videos

Row av2_grid_video_fgrid (20 × 141 frames, 768×768): 17 of 20 keep a clean background through the whole video (per prompt, the median border alpha over frames 1–140 is 0.000; step 100: 16 of 20), and the subject is solid (core alpha 0.999; the three-head split with the video readout: 0.937). The panels agree a little less than at step 100 on alpha (|Δα| mean 0.106, edge band 0.284) but match better in colour (fit residual 0.025 vs 0.045). Failures (3): the cat (0.23: starts as one full-frame cat), the steam train (0.52) and the candle (0.98: the white panel is drawn black and the alpha panel all white). A video LoRA trained on moving 2×2 grid clips is being tested on exactly these failure types (dancer, cat, coffee, candle).

Thin parts come with training: at step 100 the chef's matte includes the wok and some wisps of the flying vegetables (missing at step 50); the coffee stream and the pot are still missing from the panel alpha at step 100 (the three-background alpha has them), and the spinning top's hand appears only in the white panel (the panels disagree there). The missed share falls from 1.2% to 0.1% by step 200 and the masks agree better (IoU 0.89 → 0.94); step 300 is about level with step 200 (missed 0.27%, IoU 0.93; worst the cannonball splash, 2.7%). So far this looks like training, not the 384-pixel panel size.

Videos (step 100, row av2_grid_s00100_video_fgrid, 141 frames at 768×768). The 2×2 layout holds over the whole video for most prompts: 16 of 20 have background alpha 0.000 (per prompt, the median border alpha over frames 1–140; the three-head split with the video readout: 14 of 20 below 0.03), subject core alpha 0.987 (three-head + readout 0.937). The dancer is clean throughout, and in the coffee video the matte includes the pot and the stream at frame 70. Failures (4 of 20): the cat starts as one full-frame cat and only becomes a grid late in the video (0.33); the candle's white panel is black and its alpha panel all white (alpha 1 everywhere: 1.00); the chef 0.10 and the elephant 0.14. The panels agree less in video (|Δα| mean 0.088 vs 0.04 in images, fit residual 0.045 vs 0.02). Fix under way: a small video LoRA trained on moving 2×2 grid clips (39 frames).

First look (8:25 AM, training step 50; still training)

The layout works after only 50 training steps (row av2_grid_s00050_image_fgrid, the 20 subject-only prompts with the grid sentence): H3 draws a clean 2×2 frame with the same subject, pose and colours in all four panels.

But the 4th-panel alpha is a coarse, over-smoothed silhouette that leaves out real parts of the subject. The chef (q04): the matte misses the wok (the whole pan is black in the matte), the flying vegetables and the flame, the plate is a rough blob and the edges are cartoon-smooth. The coffee (q17): the matte misses the pouring stream and the steam, and the pot is clipped. Decontaminating with this mask cuts those parts off. Where the subject is one solid body (the skater, the cat, the cyclist), the matte is clean and fully solid, and white on white is solved: the white cup and saucer are opaque, unlike with the three-head split.

The core number is near 1 partly because the matte is a blob: it measures holes inside the silhouette, not missing parts. Missed subject (share of pixels that the three backgrounds call solid, alpha ≥ 0.9, but the 4th panel calls clear, < 0.5): mean 0.76% of the frame, worst the wave (q19, 10.7%, IoU 0.66) and the spinning top (q16, 2.0%, IoU 0.60); the reverse (panel solid, backgrounds clear) 0.40%; IoU of the two masks 0.89. The chef's wok scores only 0.7% because on the black panel the black wok also fools the three-background estimate.

Disagreement |Δ&alpha| between the 4th-panel alpha and the three-background alpha: all pixels mean 0.038, median 0.006, 95th percentile 0.208; edge band (0.02 < α < 0.98) mean 0.231, median 0.151, 95th percentile 0.689. Most of the edge disagreement is the over-smoothed matte (thin and semi-transparent parts the panel leaves out or blurs), plus thin dark contour lines of the three-background estimate along internal edges.

Open question: whether thin structures (stream, steam, flying pieces) come with more training steps, or whether 384-pixel panels (one latent patch = 32 pixels of the panel) are too coarse for them. Checked at steps 100, 150 and 200 below; grid videos follow.
